A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RankTuner work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and rearrangements.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning, out-of-distribution, code-generation, noise-diagnostic, and ablation results, including Tables 1–3 and appendix Tables 8–10.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds entropy-regime statistics, transformation-sensitivity results, and fixed-versus-dynamic exponent results in Tables 5, 10, and 12.

M1.justification: The core supervised algorithm, Relative Scale, default transformations, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Section 4.5 and new Appendix B.7 add a prospective PPO/GRPO adaptation that multiplies the token-level policy ratio by the Relative Scale. This is explicitly illustrative and unvalidated, not a change to the implemented SFT method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same mathematical-reasoning, general-reasoning, code-generation, and injected-noise coverage. New diagnostics and ablations use existing datasets; replacing the illustrated math example does not introduce a new task. RL, personalization, and multimodal applications remain future directions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained benchmark experiments is unchanged, including SFT, EAFT, OverTone, DFT, and TALR where previously evaluated. New comparisons add alternative monotone transformations in Table 10 and fixed-exponent controls K=0.5, 0.9, and 1.0 against dynamic K in Table 12.

E3.justification: Existing training settings, backbones, decoding budgets, and metrics remain unchanged. New experiments introduce transformation and exponent controls under the retained math protocol, plus an entropy-threshold diagnostic on specified benchmark subsets with CoT-plus-answer or answer-only token counting. Table 10 explicitly distinguishes its approximation configuration from final RankTuner.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of central design choices: Appendix C.5 tests dependence on the handcrafted transformations, C.7 isolates dynamic exponent adaptation, and B.5 examines coverage of both entropy regimes. B.4 also replaces the short AIME24 example with a longer Numina-CoT visualization. The existing bound-error analysis is retained and redistributed, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: The stated decoding sample counts, eight-run inference-entropy analysis and its error bars, and approximation-error summary statistics are retained. v2 introduces no new training-seed reporting, repeated-training uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results substantively extend evidence about design sensitivity and entropy regimes. Table 12 reports average Pass@1 of 37.28 for dynamic K versus 34.66, 27.40, and 23.67 for the fixed controls; Tables 10 and 5 add transformation scores and token distributions. Previously reported math, OOD, code, and approximation-ablation scores remain unchanged. New best-baseline difference rows summarize existing scores rather than improved performance.

T1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds formal definitions of the policy ratio and its Relative-Scale-modulated counterpart in Equations 36–37. The original rank definitions, probability/entropy bounds, CMVT derivation, assumptions, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged; no theoretical guarantee is supplied for the proposed RL extension.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about probability–entropy calibration, token reweighting, reasoning improvements, and complementary components. Additional experiments support these claims, while the prospective RL extension is explicitly outside the validated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 attributes robustness to the calibration principle rather than a particular transformation pair, and additional gains to dynamic exponent adaptation. It explains why minority high-entropy tokens remain relevant and qualifies the answer-only diagnostic. New discussion explicitly limits validated applicability to supervised fine-tuning and treats broader applications as future work.

D1.justification: The abstract newly provides an implementation-repository link. The new diagnostic documents loaded subset sizes, token counts, and answer-only fallback, while Table 10 explains its approximation configuration. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, and baseline implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and positioning concerning GRPO/DeepSeekMath, high-entropy tokens in RL, personalization, embodied models, recommendation, and generative information extraction. These support limited discussion of complementary or future applications. Numerous other reference edits merely update publication metadata or consolidate an existing citation.

P1.justification: The established narrative and most prose remain intact. v2 adds a Discussion section, acknowledgements, and appendix subsections B.7, C.5, and C.7, with localized explanation and cross-reference edits. It also updates the publication footer and bibliography without extensively restructuring the paper.

P2.justification: Targeted display changes add Tables 5, 10, and 12 and best-baseline difference rows to the main and cross-architecture tables. The token visualization is replaced and enlarged. v1 Figure 5 is split between v2 Figures 3 and 6, with one panel moved into the main text; other figures and tables are relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new transformation and exponent ablations address previously untested design choices, while explicit best-baseline differences make existing strengths and weaknesses easier to assess. The code-access statement and clearer separation of validated SFT results from prospective applications also help. These are limited gains: the principal results and proofs are unchanged, and the new sensitivity studies cover one backbone without additional run-to-run uncertainty reporting.
